title: On-demand Precision Modes — PRD sketch
body:
Problem statement:
- Customers want finer control over per-request quality/cost tradeoffs without creating separate model endpoints or complex routing rules.
- Current options (pin to model variant, use quantization globally, or change model entirely) are heavy-weight and cause churn for devs.
- Need a lightweight surface for app teams to express when they need higher fidelity vs when they want to conserve tokens/costs.

Idea (one-liner):
Provide an "on-demand precision" parameter that applications can set per-request (and set policy-level defaults) to trade off latency/cost vs output fidelity. Backed by: model config profiles, dynamic quantization hints, and runtime fast-fallbacks.

Goals / success metrics (90d):
- Developer adoption: 10 internal integrations + 3 external beta customers.
- Cost delta: average cost-per-request reduction of 18% for customers using economy mode on non-critical flows.
- Quality regressions: <1% of eval prompt sets flagged as regression when using mode-based routing.
- Latency SLOs maintained for balanced/eco modes within 10% of baseline.

Mode concepts (examples):
- economy: aggressive batching, 8-bit quantized kernels, prefix cache eviction for long contexts; best-effort coherency.
- balanced: default runtime (current production kernels/quant), moderate batching, preserve KV cache for session.
- fidelity: run higher-precision kernels, disable some batching optimizations, optional slow-path reranking when applicable.
- smart: heuristic that promotes a request to fidelity if flags (e.g., long-form generation, code, eval-set match) or user tier indicates higher quality.

API surface (rough):
- request param: precision: "economy" | "balanced" | "fidelity" | "smart"
- optional hints: fidelity_budget_tokens (int), require_rerank (bool), preferred_model_family (string)
- route policy: default_precision: string, scaling_rules (e.g., promote to "fidelity" for specific endpoints or user segments)

Console UX sketch:
- Per-route toggle for default precision + histogram of cost delta and quality regressions
- Traffic split UI: show how much traffic went to each precision mode and simulated monthly spend impact
- Quick A/B: enable experiment to route 10% of traffic to fidelity for N days with automatic eval hooks

User stories:
- As a product engineer, I want to set "economy" for low-value chatbot replies so we cut token costs without creating a different endpoint.
- As an ML engineer, I want to run a fidelity-only canary on new model weights to surface regressions before global rollout.
- As a platform engineer, I want to apply a policy that forces internal QA traffic to always use fidelity so our tests are stable.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- API: precision field accepted and honored by serving runtime for supported models (documented list).
- Console: per-route default_precision toggle, mode traffic breakdown.
- Metrics: cost and latency per-mode, and a quality-sampling pipeline that runs a small eval set across modes daily.

Backend approach (high level):
- Map precision -> runtime configuration bundle (model_variant, quant_level, kernel_flags, batching_hint).
- Runtime switches: light-weight fast path vs slow path; ensure KV cache compatibility between modes where possible to prevent large session degradation.
- Telemetry: tag traces with precision mode, model_variant, and any fast-fallback triggers.

Risks & open questions:
- Cache compatibility: if fidelity preserves KV cache and economy evicts aggressively, resuming session with a different mode might cause incoherent responses. Need eviction/restore heuristics.
- Observable regressions: how many eval prompts to run to detect a regression confidently per-customer? Cost of that eval.
- SLA semantics: will fidelity mode change SLA tiers (longer tails)? Need to document and surface to customers.
- Billing model: per-token pricing vs per-mode multiplier? Simpler to start with usage-based tokens + transparency table.

Experiment plan (first 6 weeks):
1) Internal pilot: implement precision param and two bundles (economy, balanced) on a single low-risk model (opensourced family). Route internal docs-bot traffic to economy and measure metrics (2 weeks).
2) Eval harness: run daily micro-eval comparing economy/balanced on 1k prompts (2 weeks).
3) External beta: invite 3 customers (SaaS chatbot, internal docs, code assistant) to opt in with console controls; collect feedback + telemetry (2 weeks).

Implementation tasks (rough backlog):
- runtime: precision flag parsing, config bundle wiring, kernel/quant switches (ENG-CORE)
- console: route-level control, traffic visualization (ENG-CONSOLE)
- telemetry: per-mode metrics, eval-runner integration (ENG-OBS)
- product: docs, developer quickstart, migration notes

Notes / brainstorming fragments (TODOs):
- Consider "micro-slots": ability to apply precision only to a subset of tokens (start/continue) — probably post-MVP.
- Investigate model families that tolerate aggressive quantization vs those that don't; maintain model-compat list.
- Add opt-in automatic promotion: if user message contains specific markups (e.g., <!--quality-->), route to fidelity.

References / links to tickets: INF-6732 (pilot), RFC:precision-modes-v1 (design), INF-6789 (eval harness infra).

Questions for next sync:
- Legal/contract: do we need to reflect precision options in enterprise contracts? (Evan to check)
- Billing: prefer multiplier or raw token accounting for clarity? (Finance + Sales input)
- UX: what are acceptable defaults for new accounts? (Growth/product)

Bottom line:
- This gives customers a simple, flexible lever to tune unit economics without model sprawl. Start small (economy + balanced), iterate with telemetry and a tight eval loop, and expand to policy-level controls and smart heuristics once stable.

Quick TODOs for me:
- Draft initial RFC outline (this doc -> RFC) — due next Wed
- Spin up pilot config on dev cluster (coordinate with Noah)
- Schedule 30m with Mika + Evan to align on eval set and billing assumption
